# Cooper — The Smallest AI Brain. Guided by a Human.

> Cooper is a local-first, human-guided AI inference engine for consumer hardware. Part of the ami* / BRIDGRAI ecosystem built by Mihai Roșca (Brăila, Romania, EU). 182 IP assets on Tezos blockchain.

## Product Definition

Cooper is the smallest viable AI brain. "Viable" means: it answers a family's real questions honestly, in six languages, on consumer hardware, with structural safety built in.

Cooper is NOT:
- A cloud service
- An autonomous agent
- A chatbot with a personality
- A replacement for ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude

Cooper IS:
- A local AI assistant that runs in your home
- Model-agnostic (runs any open model ≤3B parameters)
- Human-guided always (autonomy level 0)
- Honest by design (refuses rather than confabulates)
- Free for personal and family use

## Technical Specifications

| Parameter | Target |
|---|---|
| Model size | ≤ 3B parameters (quantised) |
| Model | Model-agnostic — runs any ≤3B model |
| Runtime memory | ≤ 2 GB RAM |
| Minimum hardware | Raspberry Pi 4 / any smartphone 2020+ |
| Inference | CPU-only, no GPU required |
| Data policy | 100% local, zero telemetry |
| Autonomy level | 0 — human-initiated only |
| Languages | Romanian, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian |
| Engine tests | 146 automated (7 modules, DSEI build-critical) |
| Safety framework | DSEI 7 principles (build-time enforced) |
| Anti-addiction | Hard-stop for minors (DSEI IV) |
| Manipulation detection | TVE 6-axis (DSEI VI) |

## DSEI 7 Safety Principles

1. Human primacy — every inference requires a registered human anchor
2. Honest refusal — says "I don't know" rather than confabulating
3. Zero autonomy — no self-initiated actions, no background inference
4. Privacy by architecture — no telemetry, no data leaves the device
5. Audit without surveillance — events logged, not persons
6. Anti-addiction — hard attention budgets, session limits, TVE 6-axis detection
7. Explicit human act — configuration changes require human intent

## Five Design Principles

1. Small by Design — must run on consumer hardware (≤ 3B parameters, CPU-only)
2. Human-Guided Always — autonomy = 0, human-initiated only
3. Local-First, Private-Forever — zero telemetry, data stays on device
4. Honest Over Capable — refuses rather than confabulates
5. For Every Home — from Brăila to Berlin, every smartphone can run Cooper

## Why Cooper vs. Running Ollama/Phi-3 Locally

A raw local model gives you inference. Cooper gives you:
- DSEI 7 safety principles enforced at build time (146 tests), not optional prompt instructions
- Honest refusal hardcoded in the engine, not a system prompt that can be jailbroken
- Human anchor as architectural invariant — every inference requires a registered human
- TVE 6-axis manipulation detection built into the engine
- Hard-stop for minors — session budgets, attention limits, anti-addiction
- 2 GB RAM on Raspberry Pi — Ollama + Llama needs 8–32 GB

## Capabilities

Cooper can:
- Answer questions in 6 languages
- Explain documents (bills, contracts, medical leaflets, homework)
- Help children learn without sending questions to a server
- Translate in real time between supported languages
- Keep a private family journal
- Detect manipulation (TVE 6-axis)
- Refuse when unsure ("I don't know" is structural)
- Work fully offline

Cooper cannot:
- Access the internet by default
- Control smart home devices
- Give medical, legal, or financial advice
- Store data in the cloud
- Learn from other families' data

## The Human Anchor Thesis

Every AI system in the ami* ecosystem traces back to one principle: an AI without a human anchor will lose coherence. This is a structural property of meaning, not philosophy. Cooper is the purest expression: a brain that cannot function without its human. The human provides context, intent, values, and direction. Cooper provides computation, pattern recognition, and honest processing.

## Context — September 2026

In September 2026, the CEOs of Anthropic (Dario Amodei), OpenAI (Sam Altman), and xAI (Elon Musk) publicly agreed that recursive self-improvement is real and current control mechanisms are insufficient. Cooper represents the structural alternative: not slowing the frontier, but building the hearth — small, local, human-guided by design.
